rows.originalSkill: Know Arrhenius expression and logarithmic rearrangement

foundExamPractice.prompt: For a first-order reaction an Arrhenius plot of ln k on the vertical axis against 1/T (in K⁻¹) on the horizontal axis has gradient −9.00×10³ K and vertical intercept 25.0. Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ln k = −Ea/(RT) + ln A. (a) Calculate the activation energy in kJ mol⁻¹. (b) State the meaning of the intercept and calculate A with units. (c) Calculate k at 300 K. (d) Explain the direction of the effect of increasing temperature on k. [8 marks]

rows.note: The question explicitly tests ln k versus 1/T, gradient, intercept A, and k at 300 K. A standalone unfamiliar direct k=Ae^(−Ea/RT) prompt is not separately certified.

rows.originalSkill: Carry out both RP7 initial-rate and continuous-monitoring methods

foundExamPractice.prompt: An unknown homogeneous reaction has these measured initial rates at the same temperature. Experiment 1: [A]=0.100 mol dm⁻³, [B]=0.200 mol dm⁻³, rate=2.00×10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. Experiment 2: [A]=0.200, [B]=0.200, rate=8.00×10⁻⁴. Experiment 3: [A]=0.100, [B]=0.400, rate=4.00×10⁻⁴. Experiment 4: [A]=0.200, [B]=0.400, rate=1.60×10⁻³. (a) Deduce the individual and overall orders. (b) Write the rate equation. (c) Calculate k with units. (d) Predict the initial rate at [A]=0.300 and [B]=0.100 mol dm⁻³. [9 marks]

A continuous-monitoring dataset for a reactant A gives time t / s: 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and [A] / mol dm⁻³: 0.140, 0.110, 0.090, 0.075, 0.064. A tangent to the smooth concentration–time curve at 40 s passes through (30 s, 0.099 mol dm⁻³) and (50 s, 0.081 mol dm⁻³). (a) Use the tangent to find the signed concentration gradient and the positive rate of disappearance at 40 s. (b) Calculate the average rate of disappearance from 0 to 80 s. (c) Explain which method determines an instantaneous rate. [8 marks]

rows.note: Initial-rate concentration data and continuous-monitoring gradients are both practised. Full experimental apparatus, choice of variables, uncertainty and true execution of RP7 remain unverified.

rows.originalSkill: Calculate complete numerical Kp from equilibrium mole/pressure data

foundExamPractice.prompt: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), 1.00 mol of N₂O₄ is placed in an otherwise empty closed vessel. At equilibrium, 40.0% of the initial N₂O₄ has dissociated. The total equilibrium pressure is 140 kPa. (a) Calculate each equilibrium amount and the total number of moles. (b) Calculate the two partial pressures. (c) Write the Kp expression and evaluate Kp with units. (d) The vessel is compressed at constant temperature, increasing the total pressure. State the effect on the equilibrium position and on Kp. [9 marks]

rows.note: Existing nine-mark practice requires equilibrium mole amounts, total moles, partial pressures, Kp expression and evaluated Kp with units. It is not evidence of independently marked performance.

rows.originalSkill: Catalysts affect equilibrium attainment but not Kp value

generalRecall.front: Does a catalyst change the equilibrium constant or position of equilibrium?
generalRecall.back: No. It accelerates forward and reverse reactions, so equilibrium is reached sooner without changing K.

generalRecall.front: How does a catalyst affect the equilibrium position?

rows.note: Exact core recall establishes no catalyst change to equilibrium constant/position. An independently verified Kp-specific catalyst explanation has not been separately signed off.
